what: ARMS-r3 section 6 (P3): per-lever attribution by kernel and by critical path, A_p (round-34 defaults) vs K_p (defaults + the 10 promoted envs), both ranks, c=1 L.A.I.L window and c=2 pair window

boots.K_p-1: results/2026-09-26-serve-r3/P3/K_p-1 (HEAD 66d5960, same docker/patch sha256, review-e14, gpu_guard rc 0)

units: ms per decode step unless named; every value is [rank0, rank1]
step_level_note: Phases and segments are medians/means of different sets and do not add exactly. Segments A-F are per-layer means x 40 inside the target graph.
category_note: Kernel time summed over all streams in counted decode steps (side streams included, so it is not the critical path). [LEVER] marks the round-3 categories; the rest are decode_timeline's stock CATEGORIES. dense_gemv = dsv41_gemv::gemv_kernel; wp_gemm = _wp_gemv_kernel or the cuBLAS 128x1 bf16 kernel at grid (2,1,1); compare_scalar<long> is split out of torch_eltwise.

main_proj.note: not on the GEMV at this M

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): p2b_moe_batched_kernel<2,1,0> (~23.2 ms/step) -> p2b_coop_df_kernel<2,1> grid 144 at ~16.4 ms/step
levers.metric: segment D (routed MoE kernel), per-layer mean x 40
levers.on_critical_path: yes: the routed kernel is the whole of segment D
levers.why: Kernel swapped on every layer (40/step, grid 144). The K absolute (15.8-16.0 c=1) is below the plan's 16.4. The c=1 delta is smaller because the coop kernel pays a larger serving tax than p2b: per call mean serve vs census bench A 551.7/543.0 vs 523.2 us (+4-5%), K 398.9/395.2 vs 353.0 us (+12-13%). At c=2: A 1058.6/1051.0 vs 1016.0 (+3-4%), K 645.9/640.8 vs 632.5 (+1-2%). In K_p the shared expert's act_and_mul + shared_down wait behind the coop grid on 100% of layers: shared_down ends 384-388 us (c=1) / 625-627 us (c=2) after the routed kernel starts, inside its tail. It is a candidate for the tax; P3 cannot isolate it.

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): b12x GEMMs at M<=8 (qkv_a, wq_b, wo_b, shared gate_up/down, main_proj M<=4, lm_head, engram wkv, wo_a) -> gemv_kernel, -1.6 ms/step in total
levers.metric: dense MXFP8 GEMM kernel time: A dense_b12x + woa_einsum, K dsv41_gemv + remaining b12x (indexer_wq_b; main_proj at M=8)
levers.on_critical_path: mostly: qkv_a, wq_b, wo_a and wo_b are on the attention-block main stream; the shared expert is not (it overlaps the router path and, in K, the coop kernel)
levers.verdict: DELIVERED on the kernel (105-110% of projection), plus -0.46..-0.51 ms/step of MXFP8 activation-quant kernels removed. The router-gate interaction below gives +0.93..+1.14 ms/step back on the FFN-prologue critical path.
levers.why: All 9 armed shapes run the GEMV (counts in dense_gemm_roles); indexer_wq_b stays on b12x (not armed), and so does main_proj at M=8. Per call, wq_b gains most (112.5 -> 99.9 us; b12x wq_b paid the largest serving tax in r3) and shared_gate_up least (57.7 -> 56.8). act_quant launches fall 226 -> 46 per step. Interaction: the GEMV shared gate_up co-schedules with the side-stream bf16 router gate. b12x never did (b12x gate_up started when the router gate ended, overlap 0). The router gate goes from 19.6/19.7 to 47.0/48.1 us (c=1), overlapped 34/35 us, and it is on the FFN-prologue critical path: +1.10/+1.14 ms/step (c=1), +0.93/+0.96 (c=2).

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): mhc_prenorm_gemm + mhc_pre_fuse + mhc_post 2.92 -> ~1.1-1.5 ms/step; 86 mhc_det_gemm_t8, 86 mhc_det_norm, ~89 mhc_det_post; no stock mHC kernels in the decode graphs

projected_ms_per_step.basis: ARMS-r3 s11; mhc-det/path_time_final.json T=4 2141 -> 1110 us/pass, T=8 2011 -> 1034

levers.metric: elapsed mHC chain per layer (attention half + ffn half, first mHC kernel start -> last end) x 40
levers.on_critical_path: yes: both halves are on the main stream between the all-reduce and the next GEMM
levers.verdict: DELIVERED at the low end of the projection (-0.98 ms/step elapsed vs -1.0..-1.4)
levers.why: Counts match the plan: 80 target + 6 draft mhc_det_gemm_t8 and mhc_det_norm, 83 + 6 mhc_det_post per step, and 0 stock mHC kernels in the decode graphs (the few left run in prefill). The kernel-time sum falls only 2.75/2.67 -> 2.07/2.02 ms/step, above the projected 1.1-1.5 absolute: in the serve the det kernels take about 24 us per sublayer against 12.9 in the bench. gemm_t8 and norm overlap each other, so the elapsed chain gains more than the kernel sum (28.6 -> 15.6 us attention half, 25.4 -> 13.8 ffn half, c=1 rank 0).

levers.metric: Engram stage span on the GPU timeline: hash DtoH end -> first rows HtoD start (median)
levers.on_critical_path: yes: the GPU is idle for the stage except for the chain the early hash moved under it
levers.verdict: PARTIAL: the span halves, but it stays at 1.1-1.6 ms against the expected 0.2-0.35
levers.why: The native gather runs in the page-cache-miss regime ([native-census], 32-call windows over the whole K_p boot). The bench measured 142 us prefetched, 274 hot and 849 cold (a prefetch miss). All 27 n=4 census windows per rank (96 rows/call): rank 0 miss/call 28.0-47.8 (median 34.4), us/call 838-1467 (median 919); rank 1 miss 42.0-50.8 (median 46.1), us/call 910-1442 (median 1018). These windows mix unprofiled and profiled calls. Prefetch v3's WILLNEED is not landing before the (now earlier) gather. buff/cache is only 3-5 GiB on both nodes while serving. The A_p span is also profiler-inflated (the host stage runs ~1.7x slower under the profiler), so the unprofiled delta is smaller than the profiled one.

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): the hash DtoH sits before the SWA/compressor metadata chain

projected_ms_per_step.basis: fusion-host 10.4, ALL chain (77 ops) hiding a ~0.2 ms native gather

levers.metric: eager chain before the hash (on the critical path in A, moved under the stage in K), median span
levers.why: The hash now runs 0.08 ms after the draft graph instead of after the ~1.1 ms metadata chain. The 75-op chain (0.35 ms of GPU span) runs under the host gather. The projection assumed a ~0.2 ms native gather that could hide only ~0.18 ms of chain. Because the gather is 1.1-1.6 ms, the whole chain hides. That is also why T2R and SWA_META show nothing on the step.

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): DeviceScan / compute_cuda_kernel (token map) 21 -> 2 per step, 168 -> 35 GPU ops
levers.metric: t2r scan/map kernel time (DeviceScanInit + DeviceScan<long> + compute_cuda_kernel)
levers.on_critical_path: no longer: EARLY_HASH moved the whole eager metadata chain under the Engram stage
levers.verdict: MECHANISM DELIVERED, STEP GAIN MASKED (0 on the critical path in this bundle)
levers.why: Per step each of DeviceScanInit, DeviceScan and compute_cuda_kernel goes from 21 to 2, and indexSelectSmallIndex and arange do the same (eager). The eager chain shrinks from 269 to 106 ops per step, with SWA_META. All of it now runs inside the 1.1-1.6 ms host stage span. It pays only once the stage drops below the chain (~0.35 ms).

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): _swa_decode_fused_kernel x15 instead of _compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel x15; no compare_scalar / DtoD / Fill<int> of the causal builds
levers.metric: SWA metadata kernel time (15/step both arms)
levers.why: The kernel swap is exact: 15 fused per step, 0 stock. In the eager region compare_scalar<long> goes 18 -> 3 per step, Fill<int> 21 -> 6 and DtoD 48 -> 33 (kernel-diff-r0.json). The 15 causal builds repeat every ~49 us in A and every ~8 us in K (step 50, rank 0), and in K all of them run under the Engram stage.

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): one _moe_prep_kernel per MoE layer instead of ~14 single-block kernels; one fp16->bf16 cast after p2b
levers.metric: FFN prologue after the router gate: router gate end -> routed start (splitK reduce, topk, prep), median x 40
levers.on_critical_path: yes: in A the router stream (gate -> topk -> 14 prep kernels) gated p2b; the shared expert finished 6-7 us before p2b started
levers.why: The r3 profile counted this glue as 0.15 ms/step 'exposed' because the shared-expert GEMMs (anchors) ran alongside it. But the routed kernel waits for the router stream, so the whole chain was on the critical path (98-100 us per layer). K runs one _moe_prep_kernel (40/step). Target-graph compare_scalar<long> goes 160 -> 0, and kernels launched in the prologue drop from 26.1 to 9.1-9.4 per layer. Part of the gain is scheduling: topk falls from ~23 to ~7.8 us per call and the splitK reduce shrinks too (router_topk -0.61, router_gate splitK -0.24 ms/step). Both ran beside the b12x shared GEMMs in A. The epilogue loses one cast: 3 -> 2 kernels per layer, routed end -> MoE AR 10.2 -> 9.4 us median.

levers.metric: candidate mask + flags kernel time (4 indexer layers x 2 kernels per step)
levers.on_critical_path: yes: indexer chain on the attention-block main stream
levers.verdict: DELIVERED (c=1 inside the projection, c=2 at 84-93% of it)
levers.why: c=1 rank 0: 80.5 -> 5.5 us per layer (the plan expected ~8-10).

levers.expected_in_profile (ARMS-r3 s6): _wp_gemv_kernel (8 per step, m 2..8) instead of cutlass_80_wmma ... bf16 16x16
levers.metric: qkv join wait on the 8 weights_proj layers: qkv_a end -> _q_kv_norm_quant_kernel start, per step
levers.why: The join median on the 8 wp layers falls from 24.2/25.2 to 0.6/0.5 us (c=1). The mean stays 12-13 us: in the comp+wp layers the compressor is now the last branch. wp kernel 88 -> 42.6 us per call (it runs beside the qkv_a GEMV; the bench measured 10-12 us alone). Side effect: _fused_save_compress_norm_kernel, which runs in the same fan-out, goes from 0.225 to 0.085 ms/step (c=1 rank 0).

reconciliation_note: Rows mix per-layer medians x 40, per-layer means x 40 and per-step medians, so they add to the measured wall only approximately. MOE_PREP and MHC_DET-ffn come from the FFN prologue medians; segment C mean delta is the other view of the same layer span.

top3_remaining_K_p.floor_note: unique experts per call from coop-moe summary phases_v2 (layer-20 census, m4 15.475 / m8 29.525), not from the serve's own routing
top3_remaining_K_p.why_left: Still the largest block: 32% of the c=1 step and 42% of the c=2 step. It runs 12-13% over the census bench at c=1 (398.9/395.2 vs 353.0 us). The shared expert tail waits behind its grid on every layer. It sits ~100 us/call (c=1) and ~75-80 us/call (c=2) above a unique-expert stream at the 231 GB/s flat-read ceiling.
top3_remaining_K_p.next: Take the shared expert off the coop kernel's tail: launch act_and_mul + shared_down ahead of the routed kernel, or fold them into the coop epilogue. Then close the gap to the flat-read ceiling (coop-moe round-4 list).

top3_remaining_K_p.item: Engram host stage (native gather, page-cache misses)
top3_remaining_K_p.why_left: 28-51 of the 96 rows per call miss the page cache (prefetch v3 misses). us/call median 919 (rank 0) / 1018 (rank 1) over the boot's n=4 census windows, vs the bench's 142 prefetched. It is the largest GPU-idle block left, and it masks T2R_DEDUP and SWA_META (0.35 ms of chain under it).
top3_remaining_K_p.next: Make prefetch v3's WILLNEED land before the early-hash gather: issue it earlier, or keep hot rows resident. Recoverable ~1.0 ms/step (c=1) down to the 0.35 ms chain, and that also un-masks T2R and SWA_META.

top3_remaining_K_p.item: Router gate slowed by the shared gate_up GEMV, on the FFN-prologue critical path
top3_remaining_K_p.why_left: New in the bundle. DENSE_GEMV's shared gate_up co-schedules with the cuBLAS router gate, which b12x never did, so the gate runs 2.4x slower. After MOE_PREP_FUSED the router stream is the prologue's critical path.
top3_remaining_K_p.next: A bf16 GEMV for the router gate ([384, 5120], 3.9 MB, ~16 us at 250 GB/s) that holds its speed next to the shared gate_up. Delaying gate_up behind the router gate is not free: act_and_mul + shared_down already wait for the coop kernel's tail, and gate_up would join them. Up to ~0.9-1.1 ms/step.

also_measured_not_top3.dense GEMV to roofline: 9 shapes at 85-96% of 250 GB/s (c=1) and 79-95% (c=2). Summed gaps to the roofline are 2.25/2.21 ms/step (c=1) and 2.79/2.73 (c=2), spread thin (dense_gemv_roofline_K). DSV41_ENGRAM_WKV_TP (KP) halves engram_wkv (1.36 ms/step on the GEMV now).
also_measured_not_top3.NCCL: target AR 80/step at 23.5/24.1 us median in both arms (c=1). AR ms/step 3.02/3.67 -> 2.95/3.06. cudaGraphLaunch host time for the target graph 3277/3397 -> 2457/2626 us. The KP comm levers (EAGER_TWIN, PM_QOS, L2_PREFETCH) target the remaining AR and startup time.
also_measured_not_top3.mHC: elapsed 29.4 us/layer (1.18 ms/step) with det; kernel sum 2.07 ms/step against a 1.11 ms bench pass; MHC_DET_OVERLAP (KP) targets it.

unexplained_interaction: P2 leave-one-out gave K vs KC (COOP alone, unprofiled) -7.66..-8.48 ms/step at c=1, while the COOP kernel delta here is -5.91..-6.11. P2 KC vs A was -6.31..-7.29, and the non-COOP share of this K_p - A_p delta is ~-8.2. So about 2 ms/step at c=1 is an interaction that P3's two arms cannot place. One candidate: without COOP, p2b_moe_batched (grid 192) meets the early-started shared expert differently than the coop kernel does. A KC_p profile boot would settle it. The bundle verdict is unaffected: it rests on P2's counted boots.
caveats: One profiled window per arm and concurrency. Kernel medians rest on 98-105 c=1 and 30-34 c=2 steps x 40 layers; step-level numbers are single-window readings, not boot-to-boot noise-gated values.

Profiled step walls (A 63.47/63.45, K 49.15/49.31 ms at c=1) sit 0.3-1.4 ms above the same boots' unprofiled L.A.I.L x3 (A 62.11, K 48.84 ms/step). Host spans (the Engram stage) are inflated the most.

K_p worker traces (all 4) had NUL bytes at exactly the 4096-byte-page-final byte after every newline (4705 / 4278 / 3739 / 2853), JSON indentation only. A_p traces and the K_p API-server trace had none. They were parsed after a lossless NUL->space rewrite (*.nul2space.pt.trace.json.gz next to the originals). The cause is in K_p's worker processes and is not identified.
c=2 windows are 2 x 80 tokens (rule fixed before the window: MemAvailable after the c=1 window was 11 GiB). The tail steps after the shorter stream ended (m=4) are excluded.

Projections are from isolated microbenches (the workstreams' unprofiled numbers). A lever's kernel can hit its projection while its step gain is masked or amplified by what runs next to it; both are reported.
